actual_source_fragments.text:
(1) In general

    The term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who-

        (A) during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages of $1,500 or more, or

        (B) on each of some 10 days during the calendar year or during the preceding calendar year, each day being in a different calendar week, employed at least one individual in employment for some portion of the day.

    For purposes of this paragraph, there shall not be taken into account any wages paid to, or employment of, an employee performing domestic services referred to in paragraph (3).

(3) Domestic service

    In the case of domestic service in a private home, local college club, or local chapter of a college fraternity or sorority, the term "employer" means, with respect to any calendar year, any person who during the calendar year or the preceding calendar year paid wages in cash of $1,000 or more for such service.

    (4) Special rule

    A person treated as an employer under paragraph (3) shall not be treated as an employer with respect to wages paid for any service other than domestic service referred to in paragraph (3) unless such person is treated as an employer under paragraph (1) or (2) with respect to such other service.

existing_cases.facts: Alice has paid $3200 to Bob for domestic service done from Feb 1st, 2017 to Sep 2nd, 2017. Bob has paid $4500 to Alice for work done from Apr 1st, 2017 to Sep 2nd, 2018.
existing_cases.query: Alice is an employer under section 3306(a)(1) for the year 2018.

existing_cases.facts: Alice was paid $3200 in 2017 for services performed for Johns Hopkins University. Alice was enrolled at Johns Hopkins University and attending classes from August 29, 2015 to May 30th, 2019.
existing_cases.query: Section 3306(c)(10)(A)(i) applies to Alice's employment situation in 2017.

existing_cases.facts: Alice has paid $3200 to Bob for domestic service done from Feb 1st, 2017 to Sep 2nd, 2017, in Caracas, Venezuela. Alice is an American employer.
existing_cases.query: Section 3306(c)(1) applies to Alice employing Bob for the year 2017.

existing_cases.facts: Alice has paid wages of $6771 to Bob, $6954 to Charlie, and $6872 to Dan for agricultural labor done from Feb 1st, 2017 to Sep 2nd, 2017. Bob has paid wages of $4520 to Alice for work done from Apr 1st, 2017 to Sep 2nd, 2018.
existing_cases.query: Under section 3306(a)(2)(A), Alice is an employer for the year 2017.

reason_from_source: 3306(a)(1) explicitly excludes domestic-service wages;3306(a)(4) explicitly limits a domestic-service employer status when applied to other services.
scope_question: Can reuse preserve the activity-specific employer qualification and payer/service identity across3306(a),(b),(c), beyond a simple subsection-specialized ordinary cache?
